rule: A template row holds a few display models (up to four, integer weights), a scale, a rank tier, a type, a family, multipliers and an optional spell-list id. Each spawn rolls a display by weight, rolls a level inclusive, and keeps each ability row only if its per-spawn availability roll passes. Abilities are then picked by weight among eligible rows, with list order as priority when all weights are zero. Few models and multipliers give many creatures because variety comes from tier, scale, level and which rows survive. Scripts re-run the availability roll by calling SetSpellList on a phase change.

data_fields.name: ability.weight
data_fields.unit: relative weight; all zero = list order

keep: Weighted display pool per template, few models many templates
Per-spawn availability roll on ability rows
Rank as a data tier, read by corpse hold and by multipliers
Per-model reach and speed as data, so a big model reads big
Ability list as its own table, not hard-coded in the AI
change: Family is a catalogue rig, not a display id
Availability and weights resolved server-side in the engine; client reads only the result
Tint and scale are data fields the client presents
D1: availability and gate rolls off by one (urand is inclusive): roll 1..100 and keep when roll <= pct; availability 0 must never appear
D2: dead modified* damage variables (Creature.cpp 1338-1346): delete; never reapply the multiplier to base damage (StatSystem 766-767 already applies it)
D3: a creature with no usable display borrows entry 1's model (Creature.cpp 698-700): reject at load, use a visibly wrong placeholder
look_test: Family card in the Pit: one rig in three sizes and tints, plus a large sibling with the same rig and one swapped wedge ability, shown idle then mid-fight at 375 wide. Dom checks: name the family at a glance, does size read as tier, does the wedge show before it lands. Second card: same tint and size, two spawns with and without the wedge row; if he cannot tell them apart in a few seconds, the swap is too quiet.
